precepts.text: The children of Judah could not drive out the Jebusites, but the Jebusites dwell with the children of Judah at Jerusalem unto this day.
precepts.point: The king of Jerusalem was already among the kings of the land which the children of Israel smote and whose land they possessed, so this fight in Judges is Judah taking the city itself.

note.label: Judges 1: Judah Goes Up First, but the Inhabitants Are Not Driven Out

precepts.why: Judah fought against Jerusalem, took it, smote it with the edge of the sword and set the city on fire; yet Judah was supposed to drive the Jebusites, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, out of the land, and could not: “the children of Judah could not drive them out: but the Jebusites dwell with the children of Judah at Jerusalem unto this day.” This verse in Judges ties back into the history we just finished reading in Joshua. The city was taken and burned, but its inhabitants were not driven out, and the Jebusites went on dwelling with the children of Judah in it.

precepts.text: Judah's border went up by the valley of the son of Hinnom unto the south side of the Jebusite, the same is Jerusalem.
precepts.point: The king of Jerusalem was already among the kings of the land which the children of Israel smote and whose land they possessed, so this fight in Judges is Judah taking the city itself.

note.label: Judges 1: Judah Goes Up First, but the Inhabitants Are Not Driven Out

precepts.why: Why was it the children of Judah that fought against Jerusalem? Because Jerusalem sat right on Judah’s border. The border “went up by the valley of the son of Hinnom unto the south side of the Jebusite; the same is Jerusalem”. The Jebusite is Jerusalem, and it lay on Judah’s line by the valley of the son of Hinnom, so it fell to Judah to take it, and it was with the children of Judah that the Jebusites ended up dwelling.

precepts.text: These are the kings of the land which the children of Israel smote, and possessed their land.
precepts.point: The king of Jerusalem was already among the kings of the land which the children of Israel smote and whose land they possessed, so this fight in Judges is Judah taking the city itself.

note.label: Judges 1: Judah Goes Up First, but the Inhabitants Are Not Driven Out

precepts.why: “Now these are the kings of the land, which the children of Israel smote, and possessed their land”. What follows is the record of the kings Israel struck down in the wars we just finished reading in Joshua. The king of Jerusalem is counted among them, so Jerusalem’s king had already fallen in Joshua’s day; the fight here in Judges is Judah taking the city itself, smiting it with the edge of the sword and setting it on fire.

precepts.text: The king of Jerusalem, one; the king of Hebron, one; Jerusalem's king was already counted among the kings smitten.
precepts.point: The king of Jerusalem was already among the kings of the land which the children of Israel smote and whose land they possessed, so this fight in Judges is Judah taking the city itself.

note.label: Judges 1: Judah Goes Up First, but the Inhabitants Are Not Driven Out

precepts.why: “The king of Jerusalem, one; the king of Hebron, one”. Jerusalem’s king was already counted among the kings of the land which the children of Israel smote and whose land they possessed. So this is not the first time Israel faced Jerusalem: the king had fallen in Joshua’s wars, and now the children of Judah went against the city itself, took it, smote it with the edge of the sword and set it on fire. Even so, the Jebusites who dwelt in it were not driven out.

precepts.point: This is a review of the history we just read in Joshua; it was not that many days ago in the reading that we covered this, and it repeats again here at the opening of Judges.

note.label: Judges 1: Judah Goes Up First, but the Inhabitants Are Not Driven Out

precepts.why:
This is a review of the history we just read in Joshua, and here it is word for word: “And Caleb said, He that smiteth Kirjath–sepher, and taketh it, to him will I give Achsah my daughter to wife. And Othniel the son of Kenaz, the brother of Caleb, took it: and he gave him Achsah his daughter to wife.”

It was not that many days ago in the reading that we covered Caleb’s offer and Othniel the son of Kenaz taking Kirjath-sepher and receiving Achsah to wife, and it repeats again here at the opening of Judges, along with Achsah asking her father for springs of water with the south land, and Caleb giving her the upper springs and the nether springs.

precepts.text: The children of the Kenite, Moses' father in law, went up with the children of Judah; these are the people of Jethro, whose counsel set up the ranking system over Israel and whose family was as eyes for Israel in the wilderness; they were always helpful to us.
precepts.point: Saul said unto the Kenites, Go, depart, get you down from among the Amalekites, lest I destroy you with them: for ye shewed kindness to all the children of Israel when they came up out of Egypt. So the Kenites departed. The Most High discriminates righteously: the people who showed Israel kindness were spared out of the judgment.

note.label: 1 Samuel 15: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice

precepts.why:
Saul gathered the people and numbered them in Telaim, “two hundred thousand footmen, and ten thousand men of Judah”, and laid wait in the valley. Then he warned the Kenites: “Go, depart, get you down from among the Amalekites, lest I destroy you with them: for ye shewed kindness to all the children of Israel, when they came up out of Egypt.”

“And the children of the Kenite, Moses’ father in law, went up out of the city of palm trees with the children of Judah into the wilderness of Judah”. These are the people of Jethro, whose counsel set up the ranking system over Israel, and whose family was as eyes for Israel in the wilderness. They were always helpful to us.

The Most High discriminates righteously: the people who showed Israel kindness were spared out of the judgment. “So the Kenites departed from among the Amalekites.”

points: After the death of Joshua the children of Israel ask the Most High who shall go up first against the Canaanites, and the answer is Judah: behold, I have delivered the land into his hand.

points: Judah asks Simeon his brother to come up with him into his lot, and promises to go likewise with Simeon into his lot, so Simeon went with him.

note.label: Judges 1: Judah Goes Up First, but the Inhabitants Are Not Driven Out

points: The Most High delivers the Canaanites and the Perizzites into Judah's hand, and they slay ten thousand men in Bezek.

note.label: Judges 1: Judah Goes Up First, but the Inhabitants Are Not Driven Out

points: Adonibezek flees and is caught, and his thumbs and great toes are cut off. He confesses it himself: threescore and ten kings with their thumbs and great toes cut off gathered their meat under his table, and as he had done, so God requited him.

note.label: Judges 1: Judah Goes Up First, but the Inhabitants Are Not Driven Out

points: The children of Judah fought against Jerusalem, took it, smote it with the edge of the sword, and set the city on fire. This verse ties back into the history we just finished reading in Joshua.

The king of Jerusalem was already among the kings of the land which the children of Israel smote and whose land they possessed, so this fight in Judges is Judah taking the city itself.

note.label: Judges 1: Judah Goes Up First, but the Inhabitants Are Not Driven Out

points: Judah goes down against the Canaanites in the mountain, the south, and the valley, and against Hebron, which before was called Kirjath-arba, slaying Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai.

note.label: Judges 1: Judah Goes Up First, but the Inhabitants Are Not Driven Out

points: Caleb offers Achsah his daughter to wife to whoever smites Kirjath-sepher, and Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother, takes it. Achsah asks her father for a blessing, springs of water with the south land, and Caleb gives her the upper springs and the nether springs.

note.label: Judges 1: Judah Goes Up First, but the Inhabitants Are Not Driven Out

points: The children of the Kenite, Moses' father in law, go up out of the city of palm trees with the children of Judah and dwell among the people in the wilderness of Judah.

note.label: Judges 1: Judah Goes Up First, but the Inhabitants Are Not Driven Out

points: Judah goes with Simeon his brother, slays the Canaanites in Zephath and utterly destroys it, calling the city Hormah, and takes Gaza, Askelon, and Ekron with their coasts.

note.label: Judges 1: Judah Goes Up First, but the Inhabitants Are Not Driven Out

points: The Most High was with Judah, and he drave out the inhabitants of the mountain, but could not drive out the inhabitants of the valley, because they had chariots of iron.

note.label: Judges 1: Judah Goes Up First, but the Inhabitants Are Not Driven Out

points: Hebron is given unto Caleb, as Moses said, and he expels thence the three sons of Anak.

note.label: Judges 1: Judah Goes Up First, but the Inhabitants Are Not Driven Out

points: The children of Benjamin did not drive out the Jebusites that inhabited Jerusalem, but the Jebusites dwell with the children of Benjamin in Jerusalem unto this day.

note.label: Judges 1: Judah Goes Up First, but the Inhabitants Are Not Driven Out

points: The house of Joseph goes up against Bethel, which before was called Luz, and the Most High was with them.

note.label: Judges 1: Judah Goes Up First, but the Inhabitants Are Not Driven Out

points: The spies see a man come out of the city and promise him mercy for showing the entrance. They smite the city with the edge of the sword, but let the man and all his family go, and he goes into the land of the Hittites and builds a city and calls it Luz.

note.label: Judges 1: Judah Goes Up First, but the Inhabitants Are Not Driven Out

points: Tribe after tribe repeats the same failure: neither did Manasseh, nor Ephraim, nor Zebulun, nor Asher, nor Naphtali drive out the inhabitants of their cities, and the Amorites forced the children of Dan into the mountain.

note.label: Judges 1: Judah Goes Up First, but the Inhabitants Are Not Driven Out

points: When Israel was strong, we put the Canaanites to tribute, but we still did not utterly drive them out; we still dwelt among them. Chapter 2 gets into what that dwelling among the inhabitants of the land brought upon us.

note.label: Judges 1: Judah Goes Up First, but the Inhabitants Are Not Driven Out

points: What we are reading is how we did not drive out all the inhabitants of the land, which the Most High had commanded us. Each tribe did not drive them out, and what did we do? We dwelt among them.
